dish: modern-style okonomiyaki on a house flour blend with secret sauce; negiyaki with beef suji; 'Hōzenji-yaki' with big seafood and pork pieces
n: Hōzenji Yokochō Yakizen (法善寺横丁 やき然)
w: Okonomiyaki counter inside the stone-paved Hōzenji Yokochō alley; Rurubu's spot page highlights its blended flour, secret sauce and Hōzenji-yaki, and Mapple lists it among Minami's 17 okonomiyaki picks for its fluffy batter and suji negiyaki.

dish: okonomiyaki pressed and lid-steamed to a fluffy rise, finished with the proprietress's mayonnaise-art drawings (buta-tama, tokujō-yaki)
n: Okonomiyaki Okaru (お好み焼 おかる, Sennichimae)
w: Shōwa-era Sennichimae okonomiyaki house of some 70 years, famous for the okami drawing Tsūtenkaku, Billiken or celebrities in mayonnaise on each pancake; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Kansai Walker's 8 popular okonomiyaki for visitors.

dish: towering negiyaki of domestic green onion on a soy-milk-and-cream batter with a Hiroshima oyster-soy negiyaki sauce
n: Okonomiyaki Sanpei Shinsaibashi (おこのみやき 三平, Shinsaibashi-suji)
w: Negiyaki specialist near Shinsaibashi known for its very tall green-onion pancakes; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Mapple's Minami/Kita okonomiyaki 17. (Separate shop from the Hōzenji Sanpei in the yokochō.)

dish: 'Pizza Ball' cheese takoyaki (8 pcs) on house-milled flour and a chicken-stock-and-milk batter
n: Daigen Amerikamura (だいげん アメリカ村店)
w: Amemura takoyaki stand of a house founded in 1963, milling its own flour; Rurubu's spot page singles out the western-style 'Pizza Ball' best-seller, and Mapple includes it in its Osaka takoyaki 16.

dish: fluffy okonomiyaki on finely shredded cabbage and gyū-suji-kon yakisoba (beef tendon & konnyaku)
n: Bonkuraya Dōtonbori (ぼんくら家 道頓堀店)
w: Lively teppan okonomiyaki house on Dōtonbori, its walls covered with celebrity autographs; Rurubu's spot page describes its fluffy finely-cut-cabbage okonomiyaki and Mapple carries an editorial spot entry (also an Inside Osaka pick).

dish: takoyaki from the Dōtonbori street-side stand
n: Honke Ōtako (本家 大たこ, Dōtonbori)
w: Takoyaki stand opened in 1972 beside the south foot of Tazaemon-bashi on Dōtonbori; ja.wikipedia notes it is repeatedly featured in travel guides with weekend tourist queues, and Rurubu includes it in its Osaka takoyaki round-up.

n: Ganso Takomasa Dōtonbori Honten (元祖たこ昌 道頓堀本店)
w: Dōtonbori flagship of the Takomasa takoyaki chain, which has its own ja.wikipedia article; listed in Rurubu's Osaka takoyaki round-up (Dōtonbori section).

dish: premium seared beef roast (炙りロース) and a fresh sashimi platter, with sake, shōchū and wine
w: Ura-Namba dining bar that was a local favourite before the back-alley district even had its name; Rurubu's Minami drinking guide lists it under Ura-Namba, and Mapple's spot page notes specialist-level Japanese, Western and Italian dishes with a deep sake/shōchū/wine list.
